title: Conditional Long SPCX — Float Normalization Entry Post-Day-1 IPO Chop; MSCI Passive Inclusion
entry: CONDITIONAL — Do NOT enter on June 12 (Day 1 IPO). Wait for the float normalization window June 16-18 (Day 3-5), when Day-1 flippers and overallotment sellers have cleared. Entry zone $130-145. Initiate 70% of position in the $130-140 zone; add 30% on a confirmed stabilization above $140 with volume normalizing below the Day-1 level. Day-1 range is expected to be $110-175 — entering into that volatility removes the edge. The MSCI passive inclusion bid begins June 13, providing technical support that should establish a floor on Day 2-3 at or above the $135 IPO price.
stop_loss: $118 daily close (~12.6% below IPO price $135) — implies SPCX is not holding its IPO value, indicating allocation quality was lower than pre-IPO demand signals suggested, OR a post-IPO market reversal sends all recent momentum-driven IPOs below water
targets: $158 — MSCI global index passive inclusion fully absorbed; Day-1 short positions have been squeezed out; retail demand flowing from investors who could not access the IPO; +17.0% from entry midpoint $137.50
$175 — First post-IPO media cycle confirms Starlink subscriber growth and SpaceX launch cadence for H2 2026; institutions that missed the IPO allocation begin building public-market positions; +27.3%
$195 — SPCX added to Russell 1000 and tracked toward S&P 500; second-wave passive inclusion creates structural demand overhang on a 4% float; +41.8%
catalyst: SpaceX (SPCX) began trading June 12, 2026, at an IPO price of $135 — a $1.75T valuation and the largest IPO in equity market history. The offering raised approximately $75B with a 4% public float. MSCI has confirmed an early-inclusion process beginning June 13, pushing SPCX into global benchmark indices within days of debut rather than waiting for the standard quarterly review. Pre-IPO demand was approximately 3.3x oversubscribed, implying a structural demand-supply imbalance that persists after Day 1 as institutions cut back in the allocation begin building public positions.
thesis:
SPCX's post-IPO trajectory faces a specific short-term dynamic that creates a tradeable entry: Day-1 IPO volatility. The combination of 4% float (extremely thin public supply), 3.3x oversubscription (pent-up institutional demand), and MSCI early inclusion (forced-buy mandate beginning June 13) creates conditions where patient entry — skipping Day-1 chaos and entering on the float-normalization dip June 16-18 — is likely to produce a better outcome than chasing the Day-1 print. Every major oversubscribed IPO of recent years exhibited a Day 1-2 spike followed by a Day 3-5 consolidation before resuming institutional accumulation.

The fundamental support is unusually concrete for an IPO investment. SpaceX 2025 revenue was $18.7B (+33% YoY), with Starlink's 5M+ subscriber base growing approximately 40% annually — a durable subscription revenue stream that de-risks the Falcon-heavy launch cyclicality. The $1.75T valuation at $135/share implies approximately 94x 2025 revenue — aggressive, but pricing a 2029-2032 horizon where Starship commercial operations, Starshield military contracts, and Starlink global expansion create a defensible multi-hundred-billion-dollar business. The MSCI early-inclusion technical bid removes the pure-valuation risk for the 2-4 week horizon: index funds must buy regardless of valuation, and the 4% float means small amounts of passive buying create outsized price impact.

The entry discipline is the thesis. By waiting for Day 3-5, we observe: (1) whether SPCX holds above its $135 IPO price after Day-1 sellers clear, (2) whether MSCI inclusion creates the expected support floor on Day 2, and (3) whether the pre-IPO capital-drain thesis (that ARKK, IWM, and RKLB sold ahead of this IPO) has resolved, leaving a cleaner demand picture. The 2% position size reflects binary IPO risk — if SPCX's Starship program misses a publicized milestone or an early earnings call disappoints, the 4% float creates the same volatility in the downside direction.

The counter-party is the SPCX bear who argues: (1) 94x revenue is undefendable regardless of TAM; any multiple compression event in 2026 hits SPCX harder than established equities; (2) the SPCX IPO ends the 'only public space play' dynamic that inflated RKLB — SPCX might trade down as institutional buyers find the reality of a public $1.75T company less compelling than private-market mystique; (3) the capital-drain thesis was about pre-IPO reallocation, and once SPCX begins trading, that pressure reverses into potential 'space is investable' inflows. All three are valid, which is why the stop at $118 is firm.
bull_case: SPCX holds above $140 through Day-1 volatility; MSCI passive buying on June 13-14 establishes a floor at $135-140. Float normalization entry at $132-138 on June 16-17. Starlink Q2 2026 subscriber count released in first earnings call shows 5.5M+ subscribers; market re-rates SPCX toward $165-175. S&P 500 consideration accelerates. SPCX reaches $175-195 by July 2026.
bear_case: SPCX Day-1 close is below $135 IPO price on high volume — indicating allocations were concentrated in weaker hands. The 'innovation IPO premium' deflates over 2-3 weeks as momentum sellers exit and no new catalyst surfaces before the first lock-up expiration. SPCX slides to $118-125; stop triggered.
invalidation: $118 daily close, OR SPCX Day-1 close below $125 with volume greater than 2x the offering size (indicates heavy institutional selling at debut), OR SpaceX issues a material revision to S-1 financial projections within 30 days of IPO

outcome.outcome_label: Thesis broken — entry zone $130-145 never triggered; SPCX surged 54%+ from IPO
outcome.note: The anticipated Day 3-5 pullback to the $130-145 entry zone never materialized. SPCX closed Day 1 (June 12) at $160.95 (+19.2%), Day 2 (June 15) at $177.99, and traded at $207+ on Day 3 (June 16). The entry condition required a correction below $145 from the $160.95 Day-1 close — unprecedented demand for the $1.75T SPCX offering made this structurally impossible. No position was opened; return is 0%.
